title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' sequel to La Longue Marche. Grothendieck is studying solution group schemes of a linearised 'loop equation'. Here rho and sigma are fixed 2x2 matrices (or elements of a rank-2 linear group scheme), standing for the images of the standard generators. G_{rho,sigma} is the group scheme of systems (alpha, beta, mu) satisfying relations of the form [alpha,rho] = eps[beta,sigma]eps (mu-1). Variants are G* (with a sign eps in mu_2, coming from the normaliser N'_sigma) and G** and G(0). Via a change of variables, these groups are identified with subgroups of B'_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma, where:
- T_rho is the centraliser torus of rho;
- N'_sigma is a normaliser of the torus of sigma;
- B'_0 is a Borel-type group containing the torus T_0 and a one-parameter group L_0.

Previous page. G* and G** were split as semidirect products G*(0)·Lambda_0 and G**(0)·Lambda_0. Here Lambda_0 = {(lambda, lambda, 1) : lambda in L_0} corresponds to L_0 x {1} x {1}. A subgroup scheme SG* ⊂ G* was then cut out by det alpha in mu_2 and det beta = 1. Equivalently, it is the set of systems (alpha, beta, mu, eps, eps') with det alpha = eps', det beta = 1 and eps^2 = eps'^2 = 1. In the (u,a,b) coordinates these become (20): det u = det b = eps' det a, with eps'^2 = 1.

This page.
1. The triples (u,a,b) satisfying (20) form a subgroup, which corresponds to SG*.
2. SG* contains Lambda_0, i.e. L_0 x 1 x 1. This lies in the eps' = 1 branch of (20) (formula (21): det u = det b = det a = 1).
3. Hence the semidirect splitting of G* restricts to SG*. Formula (22) gives SG* ≅ SG**(0)·Lambda_0, where (23) defines SG*(0) = SG* ∩ G**(0). This group corresponds to the subgroup of T_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma given by the same equations (20).
4. In (24) he notes the analogous groups without star, SG_{rho,sigma} and SG_{rho,sigma}(0). They are the intersections with SG_{rho,sigma} and are obtained by replacing N'_sigma by the torus T_sigma.
5. So the structure of SG* reduces, via (22), to studying the group (25), SG**(0) ⊂ T_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma, cut out by (20).

Next page. Since det: T_0 -> G_m is an isomorphism, the factor u is determined by det u. So SG*(0) projects isomorphically onto the subgroup of T_rho x N'_sigma with det b = eps' det a. This is the inverse image of the diagonal under (delta_rho^2, delta_sigma^2). It leads to an epimorphism onto mu_2 x mu_2 and an exact sequence.

So the page is a structural step: restricting the semidirect decomposition to the 'special' (determinant-normalised) subgroup, and reducing to a commutative or almost-commutative diagonalisable-plus-sign computation.
errors: Notational inconsistency: (22) writes SG**_{rho,sigma}(0) while (23) defines SG*_{rho,sigma}(0) as the intersection with G**_{rho,sigma}(0); the stars are used loosely. The intended object is SG* ∩ G**(0) (corrected/overwritten in the manuscript).
The containment Lambda_0 ⊂ SG* tacitly requires elements of L_0 to have determinant 1 (eps'=1 branch); this is consistent with (21) but not argued on the page.

In (23)/(25) the ambient group T_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma (with B'_0 replaced by its torus T_0) is used without justification; this is justified by the semidirect splitting B'_0 = T_0·L_0, implicit from the previous page.

ideas.what: Restriction of a semidirect product decomposition G* = G*(0)·Lambda_0 to a determinant-normalised subgroup SG* containing Lambda_0
ideas.modern_name: semidirect product decomposition of algebraic group schemes; special (det=1 / det in mu_2) subgroup

ideas.what: Description of solution groups of the linearised loop equation as subgroup schemes of products of a Borel-type group, a centraliser torus T_rho and a torus normaliser N'_sigma, cut out by determinant equations
ideas.modern_name: centralisers/normalisers of tori in GL_2; diagonalisable group schemes defined by character equations
ideas.where_published: general theory in SGA 3; the specific loop-equation groups unpublished

ideas.what: Passing from the N'_sigma version (with sign eps) to the version without star by replacing N'_sigma by T_sigma
ideas.modern_name: identity component / torus versus its normaliser

missed.claim: Part of an unpublished systematic computation of the structure of the solution group schemes of a linearised 'loop equation' (2-dimensional linear analogue of the GT relations) for given rho, sigma. The page itself is routine bookkeeping, but the overall programme of classifying such groups does not appear in the literature.
missed.quote: Pour expliciter la structure de SG*_{rho,sigma}, on est ramené via (22) à étudier les groupes (25) SG**_{rho,sigma}(0) -> T_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Linear (rank-2) representations of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type equations relate to work on GT acting on representation varieties and to Ihara/Drinfeld-style linearisations. A complete record of Grothendieck's computations could be compared with later literature, but this page adds no new result by itself.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine group-scheme bookkeeping (restriction of a semidirect decomposition to a det-normalised subgroup); interesting only as part of the unpublished loop-equation programme.
transcription_corrections: Top page number '498' is Grothendieck's own pagination (consistent with pages 293-650 of this part), not mathematical content.
Line 3 likely reads '(correspondant à : L_0 x {1} x {1} ⊂ B'_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma)', with the {1} x {1} partly overwritten.
'qui correspond au cas où (21) det u = det b = det a = 1 (eps'=1)' — (21) is the condition within the parenthetical.
In (22) the right side is SG**_{rho,sigma}(0)·Lambda_0 (double star); in (23) the left is SG*(0) and the right G**_{rho,sigma}(0); the stars are overwritten in the manuscript.
'correspond aux sous-groupes de T_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma' — B' is struck out and replaced by T_0; the struck line 'des B'_0 x T_rho x N_sigma' is deleted.
